title: Bulletin board
description: An organization's bulletin board: authors edit their own posts, authors or moderators delete them, moderators appoint and remove moderators, and the board never loses its last moderator. Data in PostgreSQL keeps the invariants.
author: Claude (agent-authored explanation; review before relying on it)
exclusions: Who the caller really is: tokens, secret handling and the mapping from token to Principal are shell conditions.
Acceptance in general: the command lemmas say what an accepted command writes, not that every valid command is accepted. Acceptance is shown only for the concrete Scenario run.
Post id reuse after deletion is not stated as a theorem. The invariant only says live post ids are distinct and below the counter.
JSON decoding, HTTP status codes, idempotent retry replies and the health endpoint are unverified shell code.
Rows written or migrated outside the kernel are not in the modeled reachable set.
Faithfulness of the compiled Rust to its Aeneas translation, real PostgreSQL behavior, durability and deployment are trusted.
Read confidentiality is not modeled: List returns every post of the tenant to any caller in it.

nodes.title: Only the author changes a post
nodes.description: Every post write made by an accepted command is either a new post by the caller under the next id, or new text for a post the caller already authored. Another user's edit request writes nothing.

nodes.title: Only the author or a moderator deletes a post
nodes.description: An accepted delete removes an existing post, and the caller is that post's author or a moderator in the state before the command.

nodes.title: Moderators are appointed by moderators
nodes.description: A moderator can appoint anyone. A user who is not a moderator can only appoint themselves, and only while the board has no moderator at all.

nodes.title: Only moderators remove moderators
nodes.description: An accepted demotion is made by a moderator, removes a current moderator, and leaves at least one other moderator in place.

nodes.title: The last moderator cannot be removed
nodes.description: Once a board has a moderator, every accepted command leaves it with at least one, for states where the invariant holds.

nodes.title: A post's author never changes
nodes.description: Across any accepted command, a post that keeps its id keeps its author. Edits change only the text.

nodes.title: Post ids are unique and below the counter
nodes.description: In every reachable board no two posts share an id, and every post id is smaller than the next id the counter will hand out.

nodes.title: Stored posts have 1 to 280 bytes
nodes.description: In every reachable board every post's text is nonempty and at most 280 bytes. Empty or oversized text is never stored.

nodes.title: No duplicate moderator entries
nodes.description: In every reachable board each user appears at most once in the moderator table.

nodes.title: No command crashes the kernel
nodes.description: For every caller, state and command, the extracted kernel returns a result: an accepted write set or a refusal, never a panic, overflow or bad index.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL data keeps the invariants
nodes.description: For the server's schema, a tenant's rows reached through accepted commands, interleaved with other tenants' commits, satisfy the invariants, and so does every snapshot a later load decodes.

nodes.title: The database holds what the kernel computed
nodes.description: Committing a write set computes the specification's applyAll, the planned SQL writes leave exactly the encoded rows of that state, and a load decodes the same state up to row order.

nodes.title: A fresh board accepts its first moderator and post
nodes.description: On an empty board, Alice's self appointment and her post "hi" are accepted with the expected writes, and the resulting state is reachable. This is shown for this concrete run, not for every valid command.

nodes.title: Refusals happen in a real reachable state
nodes.description: In the reachable state from the scenario, Bob's delete of Alice's post is refused as forbidden and Alice's demotion of herself, the last moderator, is refused. These show the permission hypotheses are satisfiable, not vacuous.

nodes.title: Every write is allowed by the policy
nodes.description: If the pre-state satisfies Inv and transition accepts a command with write set ws, every write in ws is allowed for the caller in the pre-state.

nodes.title: Policy holds on reachable states
nodes.description: Same conclusion as authorized, with the Inv hypothesis replaced by reachability of the pre-state.

nodes.title: What an accepted command writes
nodes.description: If transition accepts a command, its write set is one of six shapes: nothing (List), publish, edit of the caller's post, delete by author or moderator, promote, or demote with at least two moderators.

nodes.title: The kernel never fails
nodes.description: For every principal, snapshot and command, transition returns ok with some outcome. Refusals are ordinary outcomes, not failures.

nodes.title: Two moderators include another one
nodes.description: If moderator users are distinct and there are at least two, some moderator differs from any given user t. This bridges the kernel's count check and the policy.

nodes.title: Accepted commands keep the invariants
nodes.description: If the pre-state satisfies Inv and transition accepts a command, applying its write set gives a state that satisfies Inv.

nodes.title: The empty board satisfies the invariants
nodes.description: Inv holds for the initial state with counter 0, no posts and no moderators.

nodes.title: Reachable boards satisfy the invariants
nodes.description: Every state in Reachable satisfies Inv: unique post ids, ids below the counter, valid texts and unique moderator users.

nodes.title: Authors are kept across a step
nodes.description: If the pre-state satisfies Inv and transition accepts a command, any post after the step with the same id as a post before has the same author.

nodes.title: Moderation continues across a step
nodes.description: If the pre-state satisfies Inv, has at least one moderator, and transition accepts a command, the post-state still has at least one moderator.

nodes.title: What delete writes
nodes.description: If delete succeeds, the post exists and the caller is its author or a moderator, and the write set is exactly one DelPost.

nodes.title: What edit writes
nodes.description: If edit succeeds, the text is valid, the post exists and its author is the caller, and the write set is one PutPost with the same id and author.

nodes.title: What publish writes
nodes.description: If publish succeeds, the text is valid and the write set is a post by the caller with the current counter as id, followed by the counter plus one.

nodes.title: What promote writes
nodes.description: If promote succeeds, the caller is a moderator, or there are no moderators and the target is the caller. The write set is one PutModerator for the target.

nodes.title: What demote writes
nodes.description: If demote succeeds, caller and target are moderators and there are at least two moderators. The write set is one DelModerator for the target.

nodes.title: apply computes applyAll
nodes.description: If the snapshot size plus the number of writes is below Usize.max, the kernel's apply returns a snapshot whose list view equals applyAll on the list view of the input.

nodes.title: One write does what applyWrite says
nodes.description: If the snapshot size is below Usize.max, apply_write produces the applyWrite state and adds at most one row.

nodes.title: The store holds the computed rows
nodes.description: For a database served by the board's SQL writes reaching state s, the database holds the encoding of s, and decoding any listed rows yields a snapshot equivalent to s up to row order.

nodes.title: Invariants on PostgreSQL
nodes.description: Given a valid three table schema matching the key layout and an integer tenant value, a PgServed history of Accepted write sets yields a state satisfying Inv, and every decoded load satisfies Inv. This is the theorem the manifest requires.

nodes.title: Alice appoints herself
nodes.description: On the empty snapshot s0, Alice's Promote of herself returns Done with one PutModerator write.

nodes.title: Alice posts "hi"
nodes.description: On s1, where Alice is the only moderator, publishing "hi" returns Created 0 with the post and the counter set to 1.

nodes.title: The scenario state is reachable
nodes.description: The snapshot s2 with Alice as moderator and her post is in Reachable, built from the two accepted steps.

nodes.title: Bob cannot delete Alice's post
nodes.description: In s2, transition for Bob's Delete of post 0 returns the Forbidden refusal.

nodes.title: Alice cannot demote herself
nodes.description: In s2, transition for Alice's Demote of herself returns the LastModerator refusal.

nodes.title: Permission policy
nodes.description: allowed s u w says when user u may make write w in state s: own new or existing posts with valid text, deletes by author or moderator, appointments by moderators or a lone self appointment, demotions that leave another moderator, and counter increments by one.

nodes.title: Board invariant
nodes.description: Inv: post ids are distinct, every post id is below the counter, every text satisfies textOk, and moderator users are distinct.

nodes.title: Valid text
nodes.description: textOk t: the text is nonempty and at most 280 bytes long.

nodes.title: Meaning of a write
nodes.description: applyWrite upserts or filters posts and moderators by key, or sets the counter. applyAll folds it over a write set.

nodes.title: Board state as lists
nodes.description: St holds the next id, the posts and the moderators. Snapshot.toSt reads a kernel snapshot as this list state.

nodes.title: Moderator membership
nodes.description: isMod s u holds when some moderator in s has user u. findPost returns the first post with a given id.

nodes.title: Database invariant
nodes.description: DbInv s is Inv s together with the counter fitting a 64 bit BIGINT.

nodes.title: Row encoding
nodes.description: enc lays out the posts, moderators and counter tables. sqlA gives the table writes of each write.

nodes.title: Reachable state
nodes.description: The state comes from the empty board by commands the kernel accepted. Rows inserted by hand, migrated or otherwise modified outside the kernel are not automatically reachable.

nodes.title: Invariant holds before the step
nodes.description: authorized, inv_preserved, author_kept and moderator_kept take Inv of the pre-state as a hypothesis. reachable_inv discharges it for reachable states.

nodes.title: Only accepted write sets are committed
nodes.description: Accepted snap ws holds when some caller and command make transition return ws. db_inv only covers histories whose commits are Accepted.

nodes.title: Vectors do not overflow
nodes.description: apply_spec requires the snapshot size plus the write count to be below Usize.max. Each write adds at most one row.

nodes.title: The live schema matches the model
nodes.description: db_inv requires a valid table list of length three whose key layout equals the kernel's and an integer tenant value, and a PgServed history over modeled PostgreSQL semantics.

nodes.title: The board already has a moderator
nodes.description: moderator_kept only speaks about boards with at least one moderator. Before the first appointment there is nothing to keep.

nodes.title: Authenticated caller
nodes.description: The shell verifies an HMAC bearer token and builds the Principal. The theorems quantify over any principal, so they say nothing about whether the token holder is the real user or the secret stayed private.

sources.anchor: pub fn principal(org: u64, user: u64)

nodes.title: Tenant from the organization
nodes.description: Each organization's data is a separate tenant chosen from the principal's org. The proofs reason about one tenant's state; tenant separation itself is provided by the engine.

nodes.title: JSON decoding and replies
nodes.description: Request JSON becomes a Command and replies and errors become JSON and status codes in unverified shell code. Error to status mapping is not covered by the theorems.

nodes.title: Extraction fidelity
nodes.description: The theorems are about the Lean translation that Aeneas produced from the kernel, starting from transition. That the compiled Rust behaves like the translation is trusted, and freshness is a separate h5i app extract check.

nodes.title: Engine and PostgreSQL contract
nodes.description: The engine runs each request in one SERIALIZABLE transaction and executes the planned SQL. Real PostgreSQL behavior, value conversion and durability are trusted, and the randomized test compares PostgreSQL with apply.

nodes.title: Idempotent retries
nodes.description: Stored replies for retried requests are serialized and replayed by the shell. Their encoding and scoping per user are outside the proofs.

nodes.title: Deployment configuration
nodes.description: DATABASE_URL, H5I_APP_SECRET and the listen address come from the environment. Secret strength, database credentials and network exposure are deployment conditions.

nodes.title: transition
nodes.description: Dispatches Publish, Edit, Delete, List, Promote and Demote to their functions. List writes nothing and returns the posts.

nodes.title: publish
nodes.description: Checks the text, refuses at the u64 limit, and writes the post with the current counter as id plus the incremented counter.

nodes.title: edit
nodes.description: Looks up the post, refuses unless the caller is its author and the text is valid, and writes the new text under the same author.

nodes.title: delete
nodes.description: Looks up the post and deletes it when the caller is its author or a moderator. The tutorial's wrong user bug lives on the permission line.

nodes.title: promote
nodes.description: Appoints the target when the caller is a moderator, or when there are no moderators and the target is the caller.

nodes.title: demote
nodes.description: Refuses non-moderator callers, non-moderator targets and a lone moderator, then removes the target. The manifest's remove_last_moderator mutant weakens the last check.

nodes.title: text_ok, find_post, is_moderator
nodes.description: Byte length check against MAX_TEXT and linear searches over posts and moderators.

nodes.title: apply_write and generated apply
nodes.description: apply_write gives each write its effect on the snapshot. schema! builds apply, the table operations and decode from it.

nodes.title: sql_write
nodes.description: Turns each write into one table upsert or delete for the store.

nodes.title: Kernel for Board
nodes.description: Connects the framework to the kernel: tenant from org, transition and apply delegated to board_kernel.

nodes.title: BoardStore load and write
nodes.description: Loads the three tables with the generated schema_load and writes a write set with schema_store, which runs the sql_writes plan.

nodes.title: JSON API for Board
nodes.description: decode_command parses the tagged command JSON, encode_reply and encode_error build responses.

nodes.title: POST /rpc route
nodes.description: The router merges the framework's RPC router, which serves POST /rpc with bearer authentication, plus a /healthz probe.
